title: Reuben J’s son must have swallowed a good bellyful of that sewage. One and eightpence too much.
html_source:
Looking down into the river Liffey reminds Bloom of the story in Chapter 6 Hades about Reuben J’s son and Simon Dedalus' humorous response:

That’s an awfully good one that’s going the rounds about Reuben J and the son…There was a girl in the case, Mr Bloom began, and he determined to send him to the Isle of Man out of harm’s way but when they were both … on the way to the boat and he tried to drown … the son himself …

(Bloom is a poor storyteller so) Martin Cunningham thwarted his speech rudely:
–Reuben and the son were piking it down the quay next the river on their way to the Isle of Man boat and the young chiseller suddenly got loose and over the wall with him into the Liffey.

–For God’s sake! Mr Dedalus exclaimed in fright. Is he dead? … Not he! A boatman got a pole and fished him out by the slack of the breeches and he was landed up to the father on the quay more dead than alive. Half the town was there… And Reuben J… gave the boatman a florin for saving his son’s life.

–One and eightpence too much, Mr (Simon) Dedalus said drily.
